23.0.0.en: These are the last sermons of Christ to the multitudes. After that, all His talks were to the disciples.

23.0.1.en: Christ endured the opposition of the proud scribes and Pharisees, and used to answer their malicious questions, using that as an opportunity to teach them along with all the multitudes. But when He reached the last week of His life on earth, He wanted to expose their errors, that perhaps they would repent, and so that the people would not imitate them and fall into many sins.

23.0.2.en: God entrusted the scribes and Pharisees with teaching the people the commandments and the Law, and they taught everything with exactness, but lived a life utterly far from the commandments. So Christ instructed His disciples and the multitudes to obey the word of God that the scribes and Pharisees teach, with great caution, lest they imitate them in their wrong works, because the Pharisees neglected to carry out the commandments of God.

23.1.0.en: "They bind": He likens the commandments to loads that the Pharisees tie together and demand of the people. "Heavy burdens": He likens the people to beasts of burden, on whose backs the Pharisees place the commandments as heavy loads, until the beasts almost fall under them and lose the ability to move with them, that is, they are not able to carry them out. "With one of their fingers": they refuse to carry out the least thing of them.

23.1.1.en: Because the Pharisees do not strive to carry out the commandments, their words became theoretical, and their demanding that people carry out the commandments became burdensome, not because the commandment is heavy in itself, but because the expression and teaching of it is wrong, so they do not encourage people to carry it out, and they have no experience in how to progress gradually in applying the commandments and overcoming obstacles.

23.1.2.en: Do not teach another anything that you have not begun to carry out practically in your own life, so that you have benefited from it, and your words will be more effective. And on the other hand, you will have learned how to carry it out, and you will guide people with realistic, practical words suited to the circumstances of life surrounding you and them.

23.2.0.en: The Pharisees were not content with not carrying out the commandments, but sought honor and the praise of people. The Law commanded that the commandments be written in small script on pieces of leather and placed between the eyes, that is, to be always in a person's thought and before his eyes. But they made these bands broad, to pretend that they held to the commandments more than others. As for garments, God commanded that on their borders, that is, their hems, some blue threads be placed, that is, sky-colored, to remind them of the heavenly life. But the Pharisees made these borders large to show their piety more than others; and thus they refused humility.

23.2.1.en: The material bands dulled their minds and kept them away from the commandment, and the long, grand borders made them fall into pride, and hindered them from walking in the narrow way, that is, spiritual striving, and they even sought the grand, foremost place at feasts, banquets and synagogues. And when they pass through the markets crowded with people, they love people to give them greetings of praise and honor, and to call them by words of honor such as "my master", and by this pride they were occupied away from the love of God and carrying out His commandments.

23.2.2.en: Therefore Christ took care to be humble in all His conduct, whether at the wedding in Cana of Galilee, or His inclination to hiddenness, or His washing the disciples' feet...

23.2.3.en: In proportion to your humility, you see God and understand His commandments and love Him. On the contrary, if you seek the praise of people, you move away from His love, because you love yourself instead of Him.

23.3.0.en: Christ warned His disciples against love of leadership, authority and the praise of people, asking them to be humble, and to feel that all of the people whom they shepherd are their brothers, and that Christ alone is the Teacher and the Shepherd. The meaning is not the word "master" or "teacher" literally, but the spirit of pride and domination, because in different societies there are, of course, masters and slaves, or chiefs and subordinates, and teachers and learners. But the chief or master or spiritual teacher takes his authority from Christ, and teaches the teachings of Christ and not his own personal teachings, as is proved by the fact that the Holy Bible in the New Testament calls us to honor those in authority and submit to them (Rom 13:1-2). Likewise St. Paul says of himself that he is a father: "For though ye have ten thousand instructers in Christ, yet have ye not many fathers: for in Christ Jesus I have begotten you through the gospel" (1 Cor 4:15).

23.3.1.en: And he also calls Onesimus his son, saying: "I beseech thee for my son Onesimus, whom I have begotten in my bonds" (Phlm 10). And St. John the Beloved calls his people his children (1 Jn 2:1; 3:18; 3 Jn 4). As for the title "my lord", Paul and Silas did not object when the jailer of Philippi said to them: "Sirs, what must I do to be saved?" (Acts 16:30).

23.4.0.en: Here Christ asks the disciples and their successors the bishops, who preside over the Church and are called fathers of it, not to call anyone father to themselves, because God is their Father, that is, they are responsible for leading the Church. But the meaning is not literal but spiritual, for some fathers can call their fathers spiritually, such as the father of confession; indeed in humility they learn from all the fathers, the bishops and priests, and their fathers in the flesh. And the New Testament esteems the existence of teachers, saying: "or he that teacheth, on teaching" (Rom 12:7).

23.4.1.en: In sum, they should not act alone in authority and teachings from themselves, but by the authority of God and His word, and should not be led after any of the fathers if he teaches teachings outside the Church and Christ, like the heretics.

23.5.0.en: Then He calls them clearly to humility before one another, and whoever humbles himself, God glorifies and exalts him, but whoever is proud falls from God's sight, and He rejects him.

23.6.0.en: "Hypocrites": you pretend to lead the people to the worship of God, though in truth you keep them away from faith in Christ and from walking in the spirit of the commandment.

23.6.1.en: The Pharisees shut up the kingdom of heaven against themselves by their pride and superficiality and their distance from carrying out the commandments, and they shut it also in the face of the people by making the commandments difficult in their sight, for they loaded them with burdens hard to bear, and also made them stumble by their wrong conduct, so that they kept people away from eternal life.

23.7.0.en: "For a pretence": that is, for a personal reason and purpose, for by prolonging their prayers, people trust them and give them the guardianship of the widows' money, but sadly they are not faithful with it, but out of their greed they steal from it for their personal benefit.

23.7.1.en: The hypocrisy of the Pharisees extended, for they were not content with hindering others from entering the Kingdom, but held fast to the appearance of prayer and its prolonging to gain the praise of people, and not from love of God. And their hearts were filled with love of money, so that they exploited the weak such as widows and wronged them and took their money, and did not feel that this was exploitation and wrong, because they were absorbed in love of money and pride.

23.8.0.en: "Sea and land": that is, great effort to draw a person to the Jewish faith.

23.8.1.en: "Proselyte": a pagan who enters the Jewish faith.

23.8.2.en: "The child of hell": deserving eternal torment.

23.8.3.en: "Twofold": that is, his torment is greater in eternity, because, after he knew faith in God and was made to stumble by the Pharisees, he considers permissible his old sins in which he used to live during his paganism.

23.8.4.en: The Pharisees strive to bring one of the honorable, wealthy pagans into the faith, and they make great effort because God's help does not assist them, and then after his belief, he discovers their hypocrisy and the distance of their hearts from God, so he stumbles in them and in the Jewish religion, and departs from God, and so deserves eternal torment more than before, since after he knew the faith he denied it.

23.8.5.en: Beware of being a stumbling block to others by your sins, so that you give a bad picture of God and His Church. And do not be self-seeking in any worship, but offer it out of love of God, and you will gain the salvation of your soul, and spontaneously win those around you for Christ.

23.9.0.en: Because the Pharisees were occupied with love of money, they taught that whoever swears by the gold that he offers to the Temple is bound to carry out what he swore by. But whoever swears by the Temple may go back on what he swore by. How can this be, when the Temple is of course greater than the gold that is offered to it?! But because of their concern with collecting money, they taught this corrupt teaching.

23.10.0.en: "The altar": this is the bronze altar at the entrance of the Temple, on which the sacrifices and offerings of the people were offered.

23.10.1.en: The Pharisees also teach that whoever swears by the offering must fulfil what he swore by. But whoever swears by the altar, it is not important that he fulfil what he promised, so that they may obtain the offerings presented by the people as a material gain for themselves, unconcerned with worship, and with encouraging people in promises to God and life with Him.

23.11.0.en: In sum, whoever swears by something swears by it and by everything it contains, and this is a logical matter. And the oath was permitted in the Law of Moses, on condition that it be truthful and that its maker keep to it, but they broke the commandment of the oath by their holding fast to their material gains.

23.11.1.en: And Christ directed their attention to the spirit of the oath, which is swearing by God, the Lord of the altar and the Temple and heaven. How then do they neglect God out of preoccupation with their material benefit, and give interpretations that God did not speak? For God's purpose in the commandment of the oath in the Old Testament was to establish His people's faith in Him and their keeping away from swearing by pagan gods. Do not interpret the word of God according to your personal purposes, but submit to it and do not deceive yourself, and you will receive God's blessings in your life.

23.12.0.en: The scribes and Pharisees took care to offer tithes of unimportant plants, which might be grown in small quantities in house gardens, such as mint, anise and cummin, to appear exacting in everything. And because the leaders of the Jews benefit from the collection of these tithes, they neglected at the same time the essence of the relationship with God, which is truth, mercy and faith.

23.12.1.en: And Christ does not reject the offering of tithes, even in small matters. But let us understand the spirit of the commandment and not its literalness, so that we offer tithes in faith in God's blessing and as mercy to the needy and in clinging to God who is the Truth, and walk in mercy, truth and faith in all our life, and not like the scribes and Pharisees, whose hardness of heart appeared in wronging widows and the weak, and who refused to believe in Christ.

23.12.2.en: "These": refers to offering tithes in everything.

23.12.3.en: "Those": that is, holding fast to mercy, truth and faith.

23.13.0.en: Christ describes them as blind because they refused to see the truth that is in Him, and held fast to exactness in small matters, which He likens to the gnat, and neglected the essence of the commandments, which He likens to the camel. They used to strain water and wine lest a gnat be in it, which is considered unclean according to the commands of the Law. But with this exactness they overlook great sins, such as arresting Christ and crucifying Him though He was innocent.

23.14.0.en: Here the hypocrisy of the Pharisees appears more clearly than in the previous sins, since they care about the exacting appearance of worship, while their hearts are full of evil. And Christ draws their attention to the importance of what is inside the cup and the platter (the dish), and not only cleansing them on the outside, by keeping away from all personal uncleanness, because their food and drink, which they gathered by greed and evil, are not helped by cleansing the vessels outwardly, but by purifying their hearts. And He calls the Pharisee blind, because he does not see the truth of the matter, and is occupied only with appearances.

23.15.0.en: The Law required not touching the dead or his grave, lest a person be defiled (Num 19:16, 18), so the Jews took care to whitewash their graves, so that passersby would notice them and not touch them. Christ likens the hypocritical life of the Pharisees to the graves that they take care to paint white, so that they appear beautiful outwardly. But inside there are bones and a foul smell like the evil that is in their hearts. Their appearance is exactness and holding fast to worship, but their hearts are hard and their conduct evil.

23.15.1.en: Care for your repentance and your love for God and for others, and your works and worship will be an expression of your good heart.

23.16.0.en: Christ also rebukes the Pharisees for resisting the truth while pretending to righteousness, for they build and adorn the tombs of the prophets, and declare their rejection of the evils of their fathers who tortured and killed those prophets, though their works are as evil as their fathers', and they resisted the righteous who are greater than the prophets in their generation, namely John the Baptist and then Christ Himself.

23.17.0.en: So this speech of yours declares that you are the sons of the killers of the prophets, and not only this, but your present evils in resisting me and my disciples confirm your hypocrisy and the outward show of your righteousness, while your hearts are full of evil. And the truth is that by what you do, you fill up the cup of evil that your fathers made until it overflows, and you are condemned to eternal torment in the end.

23.17.1.en: Encourage good and help in it with all your heart and all your energy, and you will become a child of God, for everything that leads to good, God rejoices in it.

23.18.0.en: "Serpents": He likened them to them because of their cunning and their insistence on doing evil.

23.18.1.en: "Generation of vipers": because their fathers were wicked, for they tortured and killed the prophets in the past. All the preceding sins necessarily deserve the fire of hell, and all the show of worship and false righteousness does not exempt them from it.

23.19.0.en: Despite the evil of the Jews, God continues to do good to them, so He sends His messengers, whom He called by the names known for teachers among the Jews, namely prophets and wise men and scribes, to declare His voice to the people so that they would repent. But the Jews rise against them and scourge them and torture them and drive them out, and even kill them, because they are insistent on evil.

23.19.1.en: The synagogues: these are the places of reading and preaching for the Jews in all their cities, and in them they judge those whom they regard as guilty of evil and of violating the Law.

23.20.0.en: In the end, God will judge them for their resisting the truth and refusing to hear His voice, by killing His innocent men, from the first martyr in the world, who is righteous Abel, to Zacharias son of Barachias, who is the father of John the Baptist, who was killed after he placed the child John on the altar when the soldiers pursued him, saying to them: I took him from the altar and to it I return him. Then the angel of God came and snatched him from the altar, but him they killed.

23.20.1.en: And thus He depicts the Jewish nation as one person, whom God punishes for all the blood of the martyrs in the Old Testament before Christianity.

23.20.2.en: Know that God is a just Judge, so do not go on in your selfishness or your wronging of others, whatever your authority or your logical argument, but repent in humility and correct your errors, and you will receive His mercies.

23.21.0.en: This divine punishment was accomplished in that generation of the Jews by the destruction of Jerusalem and the killing of those in it in AD 70 at the hand of Titus, the commander of the Romans.

23.22.0.en: Christ likens Himself to the hen that gathers her eggs under her until they hatch and the chicks come forth to life, but the feathers of the mother hen fall off, that is, she gives her life to bring her children forth to life, as Christ suffered and died for us; and He offered His love to the sons of the killers of the prophets, but they rejected His teachings that were for their salvation, and even rose against Him and crucified Him.

23.23.0.en: The Temple was spiritually desolate because of the evil of the priests, scribes and Pharisees, and Christ left it after that, that is, He took His blessing away from it, and then its destruction was accomplished at the hand of the Romans in AD 70.

23.24.0.en: A few days after this talk, Christ was crucified and died, and the Jews did not see Him, because after His resurrection He appeared to a small number, namely His disciples and some believers. But the Jews who will believe and become Christians will rejoice on the Day of Judgment at the Second Coming of Christ, and say: "Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord" (Ps 118:26), just as the disciples and believers rejoiced in Christ when He appeared to them after His resurrection, saying the words of the aforementioned psalm; and thus everyone who believes in Christ shares with the Apostles, and feels that the blessed Christ has come and dwelt in him by faith.

23.24.1.en: Signs of the destruction of Jerusalem; the Second Coming
